operations.name: Norman Mini

expected.charges: Criminal syndicalism (California Criminal Syndicalism Act) — as a leader of the Cannery and Agricultural Workers Industrial Union, in the 1935 Sacramento trial aimed at smashing the farm-workers' union.
expected.convicted: Convicted April 1, 1935; judgment reversed on appeal September 28, 1937.
expected.sentence: One to fourteen years, imposed April 11, 1935. The prison board later fixed a three-year term. Paroled in May 1936, with sixteen months of the term remaining. Conviction reversed September 28, 1937.

operations.source: Contemporary New Militant May23,1936 p1 reports Norman Mini already released on parole: https://www.themilitant.com/1936/0220/NM0220.pdf . YEAR precision only: April11 report still places him in prison and May23 report confirms discharge; exact day and month not independently narrowed. Existing biography preserved.

expected.description: Shabazz Akeem Isiah Watson was federally prosecuted for setting fires at four Charleston, South Carolina businesses during the protests following George Floyd’s murder on May 30, 2020. He was arrested on state charges on October 13, 2020 and pleaded guilty in federal court to one count of arson on March 20, 2023. operations.name: Roger Wareham

expected.name: Roger Wareham
expected.description: Civil rights attorney and December 12th Movement co-founder, charged as a New York 8+ defendant in the October 17-18, 1984 federal RICO indictment alleging a Black liberation conspiracy to free Sundiata Acoli, commit armed bank expropriations, and bomb federal buildings. Arrested in a predawn FBI/NYPD Joint Terrorism Task Force raid and held without bail in federal custody before being released pending trial in early 1985. Trial began May 13, 1985 before Judge Kevin Thomas Duffy in the Southern District of New York; the August 1985 jury acquitted him on every count. He continued practicing reparations law and pan-African human-rights advocacy, serving as legal counsel to the International Association Against Torture and to delegations on the rights of African people before the United Nations Working Group of Experts on People of African Descent.
expected.body:
January 1985 civil-contempt custody

The June 1985 defense publication reports the seven original defendants other than Coltrane Chimurenga remanded January 29, 1985 for refusing physical samples. This distinct civil-contempt detention is recorded separately from the October 1984 arrest and subsequent criminal verdict. Actual January remand discharge remains unknown; no police rearrest or continuous custody through the later trial is inferred. The initial seven are identified from the article's named October arrestees, not from its group-photo caption, which substitutes Jose Rios for Chimurenga.

Source: Death to the Klan, June 1985, printed pages 8-9 (PDF pages 9 and 8). Complete relevant pages and captions visually checked. Existing identified photo retained.

operations.name: H. Shebeck

expected.name: H. Shebeck
expected.description: H. Shebeck was one of the 74 Industrial Workers of the World members held in the Snohomish County jail and charged with murder after the Everett Massacre. On November 5, 1916, some 300 Industrial Workers of the World members sailed from Seattle to Everett, Washington aboard the steamers Verona and Calista to support a shingle-weavers' strike and the IWW's free-speech fight. At the Everett dock, Snohomish County sheriff Donald McRae and a posse of armed vigilantes opened fire on the Verona, killing at least five Wobblies and wounding dozens. The returning IWW members were arrested, and 74 were charged with the murder of two deputies (Jefferson Beard and Charles Curtis) killed in the gunfire. Only Thomas H. Tracy was brought to trial; after his acquittal on May 5, 1917, the charges against the others were dropped. At the time of the massacre he was 24, a laborer, born in Wisconsin.

operations.source: University of Washington IWW History Project, Everett Public Library booking roster identifies H.Shebeck as IWW prisoner4833,age24,laborer,born Wisconsin: https://depts.washington.edu/iww/faces_of_iww.shtml . Historical county booking number, not BOP register.
